description.content:
# About The On Demand Rider (ODR) API provides system-to-system integration to facilitate on-demand courier delivery service requests. Each integration is scoped as a specific Brand using a ClientID. Each delivery request will be called an Order. The ODR API is supporting the following products:
## On Demand Concepts ### Client A Client represents a **single integration for a specific Brand** and acts as the **"parent vendor"**. It contains high-level information such as: * Customer's known name of the Brand/Branch * General Address of the Brand/Branch that includes Latitude and Longitude. ### Outlets Outlets are **the individual branches or vendor locations tied to the Client**. Each outlet represents the specific pickup location for deliveries. In ODR, if a client has **multiple locations**, they **can all be configured under the same parent vendor**. Outlet details include: * Branch vendor name * Address of outlet with latitude and longitude.   **Note**: In ODR, **all orders should be sent from an Outlet**. Even if the client has only one location, the order should still originate from the Outlet and not the parent vendor. ## Ordering Steps 1. The Sender address must be specified when submitting an Order. 2. The Sender latitude and longitude will be used to find the matching Branch/Outlet. ### Supported Payment Methods | Payment Method | Description | | - | - | | PAID | Order has been fully paid already and courier will not collect any amount from the end customer | | CASH_ON_DELIVERY | Courier will collect payment (order amount) from the end customer upon delivery | | CARD_ON_DELIVERY | Payment by credit card upon receipt of the order | ## API Endpoints and URLs Below are the API endpoints for each brand and country: - Production URLs use DH-friendly domains when available. - Staging URLs https://api-infra-eu-central-1.stg.ondemandrider.net/ug | --- # Getting Started ## 1. Provide a public key These are the steps to start using the ODR API: 1. Generate Key Pair (Private Key and Public Key) to support secure communication with the ODR API. Follow these commands on a terminal: ```bash # Generate private key # output: client.pem file openssl genrsa -out client.pem 2048 # Generate public key from the generated private one # input: client.pem file # output: client.pub file openssl rsa -in client.pem -pubout > client.pub ``` Or, follow these steps: 1. Open a browser and access [this Online RSA Generator](https://emn178.github.io/online-tools/rsa/key-generator/) 2. Select key length to 2048 bit, and click the Generate Key Pair button. 3. Copy and save the Private Key to a file with .pem extension (e.g. client.pem). 4. Copy and save the Public Key to a file with .pub extension (e.g. client.pub). 2. The ODR representative will provide you with `ClientID`, `KeyID` and `Scope` that your service will need to generate an Access Token for the ODR API. | Attribute | Description | Example | | - | - | - | | ClientID | Your service identifier| pandago:sg:00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 | | KeyID | Your public key identifier| 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 | | Scope | Access scope of your service| `pandago.api.{country code}.*` (ex: `pandago.api.pt.*`) | ## 2. Generate signed JWT Generate assertion as a signed token in Javascript Web Token (JWT) format. This is the payload structure of the token: ``` { "alg":"RS256", "typ":"JWT", "kid": "{{KeyID}}" } . { "iss":"{{ClientID}}", "sub":"{{ClientID}}", "jti":"{{random uuid (e.g. caa56777-4e88-4c59-be70-3ae513fd2e00)}}", "exp":{{unix timestamp in the future (e.g. 1894712882)}}, "aud":"https://sts.deliveryhero.io" } ``` And use your Private Key to sign the token. 💡 **Tips** 💡 * Always use `https://sts.deliveryhero.io` for `aud` key, in both testing and prod environments * For the `exp` key, just get a future timestamp (ex in 1 year) with [unixtimestamp.com](https://www.unixtimestamp.com/index.php) ## 3. Get a JWT access token Follow the instructions to call [the auth endpont](#tag/Authentication)
